skills.name: codebase-explore
skills.description: Use when gathering background codebase context as part of a larger workflow, such as the brainstorming or planning explore step, or before modifying unfamiliar code to understand architecture and structure. Not for a direct one-off question (use codebase-ask), a named symbol's callers/callees (use codebase-graph), the effect of a diff (use codebase-impact), capability mapping (use codebase-capabilities), boundary/seam inspection (use codebase-seams), the architecture map or rules (use codebase-architecture), or a guided reading order (use codebase-tour).

skills.name: codebase-ask
skills.description: Use when the user asks a direct natural-language question about the codebase: 'where does X happen', 'how does X work', 'anything similar to X', 'what should I know before adding X'. Not for ambient context during brainstorming/planning (use codebase-explore), call graphs of a named symbol (use codebase-graph), what a diff affects (use codebase-impact), capability mapping (use codebase-capabilities), boundary/seam inspection (use codebase-seams), the whole-system architecture or its rules (use codebase-architecture), or a reading order (use codebase-tour).

skills.name: codebase-index
skills.description: Use when the codebase index must be built, refreshed, or linked across repositories: 'index this repo', 'reindex', 'index is stale', 'link repos', or when other codebase skills report no index. This only builds or links the index; to answer questions use the other codebase skills (ask, graph, impact, architecture, tour, and so on).

skills.name: codebase-impact
skills.description: Use when the user asks what recent code changes affect: 'what did my changes break', 'blast radius of this diff', 'what might break', 'which tests are affected'. Works from a git diff or base SHA. Not for questions about code that has not changed (use codebase-ask) one symbol's callers (use codebase-graph), risky frequently changed code (use codebase-hotspots), or unused code (use codebase-dead-code).

skills.name: codebase-graph
skills.description: Use when the user names a specific symbol and wants its relationships: 'who calls X', 'what does X call', 'call graph for X', 'dependencies of X'. Supports depth and direction. Not for general how/where questions (use codebase-ask) or diff-based impact (use codebase-impact).

skills.name: codebase-capabilities
skills.description: Use when the user wants to discover or inspect functional capabilities in one or more codebases: 'what capabilities exist', 'map capabilities', 'how is capability X structured', 'trace capability X across repos', 'compare capabilities between project A and B'. Not for a single symbol's immediate callers/callees (use codebase-graph), domain entities and their owners (use codebase-domain), or boundary coupling inspection (use codebase-seams).

skills.name: codebase-seams
skills.description: Use when the user wants to identify, inspect, or audit architectural seams and boundaries within a codebase or across indexed repositories: 'what are the seams', 'find leaky seams', 'show the boundary between X and Y', 'where can we split or decouple X', 'how does repo A integrate with repo B'. Not for tracing a single symbol's call tree (use codebase-graph) diff blast radius (use codebase-impact), or the whole-system component map and rules (use codebase-architecture).

skills.name: codebase-architecture
skills.description: Use when the user wants the whole-system architecture of a codebase or several linked repos, or wants a planned change checked against architecture rules: 'show the architecture', 'what are the components and layers', 'does this break our architecture rules', 'check ARCHITECTURE.md'. Not for one boundary's coupling in depth (use codebase-seams), behaviour corridors (use codebase-capabilities), or a symbol's callers (use codebase-graph).

skills.name: codebase-tour
skills.description: Use when the user asks where to start reading a codebase or wants a guided reading order: 'give me a tour', 'where do I start', 'onboard me to this repo', 'walk me through the X area'. Not for background context inside another workflow (use codebase-explore), a specific question (use codebase-ask), or the component map (use codebase-architecture).

skills.name: codebase-domain
skills.description: Use when the user wants the main concepts or entities of a codebase and who owns them: 'what are the core domain types', 'explain the data model', 'who creates or changes X', 'which component owns X'. Not for behaviour or execution corridors (use codebase-capabilities), one symbol's call graph (use codebase-graph), or the component map (use codebase-architecture).

skills.name: codebase-hotspots
skills.description: Use when the user wants the risky, frequently changed parts of a codebase: 'where are the hotspots', 'what code changes most', 'what is riskiest to touch', 'where should we refactor first'. Not for what a specific diff affects (use codebase-impact) or unused code (use codebase-dead-code).

skills.name: codebase-dead-code
skills.description: Use when the user wants unused code found: 'find dead code', 'what can I delete', 'unused functions or exports', 'is X still used anywhere'. Not for what a diff affects (use codebase-impact) or risky frequently changed code (use codebase-hotspots).

commands.name: codebase-ask
commands.description: Ask a question about the codebase. <question>

commands.name: codebase-index
commands.description: Build, refresh, or link the codebase index. [--mode full|moderate|fast|cross-repo-intelligence] [--link <project|*>]

commands.name: codebase-impact
commands.description: Show what your recent changes affect. [--base <sha>]

commands.name: codebase-graph
commands.description: Show a symbol's callers and callees. <symbol> [--depth 1-5] [--direction inbound|outbound|both]

commands.name: codebase-capabilities
commands.description: Map functional capabilities and execution corridors. [<capability>] [--project <name>...] [--depth 1-5]

commands.name: codebase-seams
commands.description: Inspect architectural seams and coupling across packages or repos. [<source> [<target>]] [--project <name>...]

commands.name: codebase-architecture
commands.description: Recover the architecture and check it against your rules. [--check] [--project <name>...]

commands.name: codebase-tour
commands.description: Get a guided reading order for a codebase or area. [<area>]

commands.name: codebase-domain
commands.description: Map the main domain entities and who owns them. [<concept>]

commands.name: codebase-hotspots
commands.description: Rank files by churn and risk. [--since <date>] [<path>]

commands.description: Find code nothing uses, with each candidate verified. [<path>]
